pages.head: Welcome
pages.html:
Welcome

Keys and Doors is a Starter: a small game that shows a few Game-Maker ideas, with signs in the levels that say what you are looking at. It has two short levels and takes a couple of minutes to finish.

Play it first. Then open it in Game-Maker (Edit a copy on the home page keeps the original safe) and read the pages below, which say where each thing in the levels is made.

The keys

Left and Right walk. Space jumps. Up and Down climb a ladder. Walk into the door at the end of a level to go on. There is nothing to fight and nothing that hurts.

pages.head: Level 1: One Key, One Door
pages.html:
Level 1: One Key, One Door

The A KEY ADDS TO A COUNTER sign stands beside a key. Touch the key and you carry one. Further on, the THE DOOR NEEDS 1 KEY sign warns of a locked door in a brick wall. Walk into it with the key and it opens, and you carry none again. Walk into it with no key and it stays shut. The EXIT → sign points to the way out.

Coins are worth ten points each. There are eight, and a key is worth 25.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 1 is made

  • The key. Open keys.bbl in the blocks editor and pick the key block. On its Touch tab, Effect counter is set to counter 20 and Effect amount to 1, and Becomes block is sky, so the key is gone once you have it.
  • The locked door. The gate block is solid on every side, so it stops you. Its Effect counter is also counter 20, but its Effect amount is −1. A counter from 20 up will not go to zero or less, so a touch that cannot be paid for does nothing. With a key, the touch pays one, and Becomes block turns the door into sky.
  • Why you cannot jump over it. The door is one block high, with an arch block above it that you walk under, and a wall of brick from there up to the top of the level. There is no way around.
  • The counter itself. Open hero.chr in the character editor. Counter 20 starts at 1, which the game shows as none carried.
  • The signs. Each sign is a few ordinary blocks side by side, with the words drawn in their pictures. Change the words in the blocks editor and play again.
  • The exit. A scene link joins the door at the end to the next level. Open keys.gam in the scenes editor and look at the links of the One Key, One Door scene.

pages.head: Level 2: Two Keys, Two Doors
pages.html:
Level 2: Two Keys, Two Doors

Two doors, and each wants its own key. A gold key lies on the ground by the GOLD KEY, GOLD DOOR sign. A silver key sits on a ledge high above the start, where you can see it but not yet reach it. Take the gold key and open the gold door. Behind it a ladder climbs to the ledge: climb up, walk back along the ledge for the silver key, and climb down again. The silver key opens the silver door, and the exit is beyond.

There are eleven coins, some of them along the ledge.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 2 is made

  • A second counter. A silver key adds to counter 21, a gold key to counter 20. Each door spends from its own counter, so a gold key never opens a silver door. Open keys.bbl and compare the key, keySilver, gate and gateSilver blocks. Counter 21 also has to start at 1 in hero.chr.
  • A door can need more than one key. Change Effect amount on a door to −2 and it takes two keys. A counter holds one more than the keys you carry, so with two keys a door that costs two just works.
  • The ledge. Open two.map in the map editor. The ledge is a row of grass over dirt. It runs over the gold door, so the only way up is the ladder on the far side of it.
  • The ladder. The ladder block has no gravity pull and no solid side, so you stay on it and Up lifts you.
  • The exit. The last door links to the The End scene in keys.gam, which plays the ending.

pages.head: Make it yours
pages.html:
Make it yours

Try one change at a time, and play after each:

  • Move a key somewhere harder to reach.
  • Make the gold door take two keys, and put a second gold key in the level.
  • Draw a third kind of door and key, with counter 22 (set it to start at 1 in hero.chr).
  • Draw a platform with the plank block: solid on top only, so you can jump up through it.

The home page's Starters tab has more small games like this one.
